log.msg: FIVE SENTENCES before: what=a directory of three browsing tools for the framework's building blocks (Lists, Answers, Cards); use=click one of the three cards, it opens as a new column to the right; goal=find a specific page, layout or demo by walking the taxonomy, or understand what borrowing a page costs; hard=2/5 -- the three cards are self-explanatory once you read them, but the intro text uses the term foreign page before it means anything and every single card in the whole realm (this index, the Lists index, and all nine Column-shapes cards) is icon+title+description text with zero picture, so nothing here shows what any of it actually looks like; better=give the three top cards and the six-list index real static pictures of what is inside them instead of an icon, since a gallery whose own cards carry no image is the one place on the site that most needs one.

ALTERNATIVE LAYOUT tried: replaced this.previews() (tile wall, one of the approved five, and the exact shape approved/page.js names for a gallery) with this.tabs().ac('vertical') -- the paging-vocabulary surface-swap option, using the framework's own tabs building block that this realm curates in its own Lists index. Built it, ran it live at 1280 and 3440. Result: broken, not better. tabs() mounts each child via its full render(), which draws that child's OWN page-column-head chrome (title bar + close X) -- so picking Lists produced a small bordered box floating mid-page with a second nested title bar and its own close button, at roughly 460px wide against the page's 1152px column (3440), i.e. LESS width used, not more, and a confusing double-frame a stranger would read as a bug. Measured at 3440: right edge 1583px unchanged (still the columns-row cap), column height 852px unchanged from the tile wall -- no gain on width, dead space, or height, and a real visual regression. REVERTED to previews(). Verdict: tabs() is built for a set of PEER views inside one page, not for mounting three already-independent Page children that still expect to draw their own column chrome; the tile wall stays because it is the one shape here that does not double the frame.

MORE VISUAL: the realm-wide finding -- every card in Gallery (this index's 3, Lists' own 6, and all 9 Column-shapes cards) was icon+title+description text, zero pictures, in a realm whose whole job is showing what the framework can be made of. Fixed the two that are this realm's own (Lists/Answers/Cards children are gallery's, not foreign): generated three static thumbnail jpgs with a scratchpad Playwright script (make-thumbs.mjs) -- Lists gets a shot of its own Column-shapes wall, Answers gets the live Import-meter readout after pressing the button, Cards gets its own before/after restyle pair -- and gave each child page.js a preview(nav) override that draws the picture via img(), never a live instance (preview_card's documented pattern, core/Page/Page.class.js:495). Also found and fixed a second, worse instance one level in: Lists' OWN index (Building blocks/Navigation/The box/Recipes/Column shapes/Layouts) had no index:true and no previews() call at all -- it fell through to Page.class.js's DEFAULT plain-link rail, the barest possible list, not even a card. Added index:true + this.previews(), gave the list() factory a description (the existing blurb, markdown stripped) and a fitting icon each, and gave Lists itself a preview() thumb (a shot of the Column-shapes wall standing in for all six).

NUMBERS at 3440: width used 33.5% -> 33.5% (1583-432)/3440, unchanged -- the column's own body sits at 432..1583px both before and after; the 1857px band past it is the known site-wide columns-row cap, not this page. Page height (.page-column-body rect/scrollHeight): 852px -> 852px at 3440, 860px -> 860px at 1280, unchanged in both cases because that box floors at the viewport height regardless of content (neither version scrolls) -- the real change is density, not extent: three thumbed cards now fill roughly the same box three plain-text cards did, with a picture instead of nothing below the fold. Invariants: no content at x:0 (pass, column starts at 432px past the rails) -- no prose past the measure (pass, the two md() sentences wrap well inside the 64em column) -- no framed box touching a container edge (pass, .page-previews keeps the standard gutter on all three cards, before and after).
PERSISTENCE: grep -rn for store() or localStorage under public/imagine/gallery/ -- zero matches. Gallery persists nothing: no baseline() import needed.

UI-TEST: drove /imagine/gallery/ at 1280 headless (Playwright, gallery-click.json in the scratchpad) -- clicked the new Cards thumb card, confirmed via eval that location.pathname became /imagine/gallery/cards/ and the crumb bar read Imagine > Gallery > Cards, zero console errors across all 6 steps. Separately ran a fresh visit-all-four-pages pass (gallery, lists, answers, cards) at both 1280 and 3440 in one browser context each: zero console errors at either width.

FIVE SENTENCES after: what=a directory of three browsing tools for the framework's building blocks, each one now shown by a real picture of what it contains rather than an icon; use=click a card -- Lists' own wall, the live import-cost readout, or the card-restyle comparison -- it opens as a new column to the right, exactly as before; goal=find a specific page, layout or demo by walking the taxonomy, or see what borrowing a page costs and looks like without opening it; hard=1/5 -- the three cards now show their own content, so a stranger can tell Lists from Answers from Cards before reading a word, and the one remaining friction (the term foreign page in the intro) is a vocabulary word the page itself defines one sentence later; better=carry the same treatment one layer deeper, a small still for each of the 42 individual paths inside the six lists, which the realm's own readme.md flags as too costly to import eagerly today -- a cheap pre-rendered sprite sheet, not a live import, would fix that without touching the lazy-loading design the doc/decisions.md already defends twice.

assign.outcome: **Gallery's cards now show the thing instead of naming it — Lists, Answers and Cards each carry a real picture, and Lists' own bare six-item list became a card wall.** Tried the paging-vocabulary tab-swap as an alternative to the tile wall on the landing page; reverted it (measured: no width/height gain, and it drew a second column-chrome nested inside the first).
